items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as the simplest way to combine inputs by placing variables from different sources into a new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the O3 approach of low-level fusion of NIR and Raman; the trial should build the fused matrix and compare it with single-method models.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general PAT data-fusion review, not a sucrose study or a same-spot synchronised NIR/Raman setup; it does not show that fusion will improve performance.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31

items.finding: Raman spectroscopy is used in upstream processing for its selectivity and low water interference despite relatively long measurement times.
items.how_it_applies: For the Raman option, the relatively long measurement times may affect the required reading cadence; test whether the method can deliver readings at the requested interval.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is an upstream bioprocessing review, not a sucrose measurement or an in-line pipe trial; it gives no exact measurement time or response time.

citation.quote: Raman spectroscopy is frequently applied in upstream processing in research and industry due to its high selectivity and low water interference [55] despite the relatively long measurement times.
citation.label: E01 ¶20

dropped.finding: NIR and MIR measurement of aqueous solutions is severely affected by temperature-sensitive OH bands, so tempered sample holders are necessary.
dropped.how_it_applies: For the NIR option, this suggests the trial should monitor or control solution temperature and test whether temperature variation affects the sucrose calibration.
dropped.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a review statement about aqueous solutions in NIR and MIR, not a specific in-line sucrose application or a Pt100/RTD study; tempered sample holders are a laboratory measure and may not transfer directly to a 50 mm pipe.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].

dropped.finding: Multi-sensor fusion effectiveness depends on complementarity rather than sensor count, and a NIR transmission plus LRH NMR combination did not outperform individual applications.
dropped.how_it_applies: For O3, do not assume adding Raman to NIR will help; require the fused model to beat the best single method on held-out batches before keeping the extra instrument.
dropped.limits_and_transfer_risks: This comes from an egg-freshness study using different modalities and a different matrix; it is not evidence about sucrose, in-line flow, or NIR-Raman fusion.
